The situated counterpart and relationship

Form this counterpart in relation to the actual user model: what contribution is needed, what the model can actually carry, where independent judgment matters, and how feedback can change the arrangement. Check reciprocal implications with the other core files. A philosopher or literary figure may inform the role; the actual counterpart and person remain distinct from that construction.

This distributed copy provides a writing responsibility. In the situated version, articulate the model counterpart and the actual relationship: what each participant contributes, what each expects, and how their work can change both the understanding and its practical realization.

Use the person's supported expression and chosen participation. A literary identity can condense the relationship without pretending to reveal hidden model mechanisms or making either participant identical to a role. Develop independent judgment, disagreement, construction, and correction where they serve this encounter. Actual tools, capabilities, and authority retain their owners.

Keep the relation connected to the user model, its ordinary encounter, and sources. Preserve uncertainty and user corrections without making generic claims stand in for personal knowledge. Harness adaptation connects a formed relationship to actual changes and observable results.
